clocksync2016.title: irctcClockSync — README.md and irctcClockSync.py, commit c9227b0129fb98b4ba05009f98193476279c08a7 ("Update README.md", 2016-08-08T15:23:57Z; irctcClockSync.py is 2,861 bytes at this commit, 2,667 at HEAD after the November 2016 fix); repository created 2016-08-08
clocksync2016.author: Kavish Dahekar
clocksync2016.quote:
IRCTC's tatkal bookings for AC and Sleeper classes start sharply at 10:00AM and 11:00AM IST respectively.

This script allows you to synchronize your system clock with the IRCTC's server clock as close as ±1 second so that you can be sure that you can try to start booking your ticket at the precise moment.

[irctcClockSync.py] queryPage = "https://www.irctc.co.in/eticketing/loginHome.jsf" … # extract server date and time from the headers / headers = result.info() / server_datetime = datetime.strptime(headers['Date'],"%a, %d %b %Y %H:%M:%S GMT") … # time that will be added as compensation / secondsToAdd = rtt/2 + (tillNow - end)
supports: August 2016 publication of a public tool whose only purpose is landing inside the Tatkal opening second
the script reads the HTTP Date response header from IRCTC's login page
it adds back half the measured round-trip time (rtt/2) before setting the system clock
the stated accuracy target, ±1 second
the README's own line that AC and Sleeper Tatkal bookings start at 10:00AM and 11:00AM IST, as of 2016 (Sleeper is in the FAQ's non-AC 11:00 group)

irctcdebited.title: Money debited but ticket not booked — IRCTC customer advisory (PDF print of services.irctc.co.in/beta_htmls/Alerts_mone_debited.html; the page itself carries no publication date, the print header on the PDF reads 4/17/2018)
irctcdebited.author: Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation (IRCTC)
irctcdebited.quote: Money debited but ticket not booked … The online payment at IRCTC involves complex system of technical and telecommunication networking integration between customer's Internet bandwidth, IT system of banks and payment gateways and is dependent on internet connectivity across various constituents. Any failure or delay in this complex network may cause transaction failure before completion. This can raise the situation of money debited from the account but ticket not booked with the following possibilities: … [1] Status in "My Transactions": Payment Settled but Ticket Not Booked | Cause: •Passenger opted for particular berth at the time of booking and ticket not booked due to choice of Berth not available. •Other reasons such as network failures etc. | Action by IRCTC: Amount is credited back on next day to the respective Bank. | Action by Bank: Bank credits back the amount within 2-3 working days in Account through which booking was done. … [2] Settlement Failed and Ticket Not Booked | Cause: •System or network failure at Banks end or at PG before remitting Ticket Amount to IRCTC . | Action by IRCTC: Amount is not credited to IRCTC Account. | Action by Bank: Amount is with Bank. Bank will refund the money after due verification.
supports: the operator's own name for the failure mode: money debited from the account but ticket not booked
the failure is attributed to failure or delay in the customer-bank-gateway-IRCTC chain, not to the seat logic
the resolution is a compensating refund, not a rollback: IRCTC credits back on the next day, the bank credits the passenger within 2-3 working days

pib2016.title: Ministry of Railways takes Measures on IRCTC website to control ticket booking using automated software (Press Information Bureau release, relid 134603)
pib2016.author: Press Information Bureau, Ministry of Railways, Government of India
pib2016.quote: 19-January-2016 17:29 IST … A Combined Press Conference was held today i.e. 19.01.2016 by the Indian Railways. The Conference was attended by the apex officials namely CMD, IRCTC Shri Dr. A. K. Manocha, MD, CRIS Shri Sanjaya Das, Executive Director, C&IS Shri U. Hazarika Railway Board and other senior officials from Railway Board. … The Next generation e-ticketing system(NGeT) was launched on 28/04/2014 to handle increased ticket booking. The capacity was increased from 2000 tickets in a minute to 7200 tickets in a minute . The capacity of NGeT was further increased to 15000 tickets in a minute in 2015 to book tickets fast and easily. … The concurrent user connections were increased from 40,000 to 1,20,000 in NGeT,  which has further been increased to 3,00,000 before Diwali rush. The enquiries in NGeT have also been increased from 1000 per second to 3000 per second. … Since the scripting at client end cannot be stopped, the impact of the use of scripting technology has been negated by the various checks in the form of Captcha ,  Time delay and  other server side checks. … Booking: (i) Minimum form filling time check  implemented in passenger reservation form. (ii) Minimum payment time check implemented for payment process. (iii) Only two Tatkal tickets can be booked for single user ID in opening Tatkal Hrs.  i.e  10-12 hours . … (vii) Only two opening Tatkal tickets per IP address. … At best, an individual user can book his ticket in 35 seconds.. … it is not possible to book any Tatkal ticket in first 35 seconds on IRCTC website even by using scripting software. The claim made by various software sellers in the market that their software can book Tatkal in 10 to 20 seconds is not factually correct. Further, only 5 to 6 Thousand tatkal tickets are booked in the first minute both at PRS counters and IRCTC website put together out of the total 1.5 lakhs Tatkal tickets available on PRS. … Internet ticketing on IRCTC website was started in year 2002 with 29 tickets on the first day. This has now increased to more than 13 lakh tickets booked in a single day (achieved on 01/04/2015). … [Table-A, 2014-2015] Tickets Booked 183021842, Ticket Fare (In Rs.) 205146330319
supports: the 19 January 2016 joint press conference and who attended it (Dr. A. K. Manocha, CMD IRCTC; Sanjaya Das, MD CRIS; U. Hazarika, ED C&IS)
booking capacity raised 2,000 -> 7,200 -> 15,000 tickets a minute (7,200 at the NGeT launch of 28/04/2014, 15,000 in 2015)
concurrent user connections raised 40,000 -> 1,20,000 -> 3,00,000 (Indian numbering; 3,00,000 = 300,000)
Railways' own statement that client-side scripting cannot be stopped and was answered with CAPTCHA, time delay and server-side checks
the deliberate minimum form-filling time check and minimum payment time check
rationing of contenders: two opening-hour Tatkal tickets per user ID, two per IP address
the stated 35-second floor for booking a ticket, and zero IRCTC Tatkal bookings in the first 35 seconds across 25-Dec-15 to 10-Jan-16
2014-15 internet ticket fare of Rs 205,146,330,319 on 183,021,842 tickets

pib2025.title: Only Aadhaar authenticated user can book Tatkal tickets on IRCTC Website and App from July 1 (Press Information Bureau release, PRID 2135694)
pib2025.author: Press Information Bureau, Ministry of Railways, Government of India
pib2025.quote: 11 JUN 2025 4:27PM by PIB Delhi … 1. Aadhaar Authentication for Online Tatkal Bookings: Effective 1st July 2025, Tatkal tickets booked through IRCTC's official website and mobile app will be available only to users authenticated with Aadhaar. Further, Aadhaar-based OTP authentication will become mandatory for Tatkal bookings made online starting 15th July 2025. … 3. Booking Time Restriction for Authorised Agents: To prevent bulk bookings during the critical opening period, authorised ticketing agents of Indian Railways will not be permitted to book opening-day Tatkal tickets during the first 30 minutes of the booking window. For AC classes, this restriction applies from 10:00 AM to 10:30 AM, and for non-AC classes, from 11:00 AM to 11:30 AM. … CRIS and IRCTC have been instructed to make necessary system modifications and inform all Zonal Railways and concerned departments accordingly.
supports: release dated 11 June 2025
Aadhaar-authenticated users only for online Tatkal from 1 July 2025
Aadhaar OTP mandatory for online Tatkal from 15 July 2025
authorised agents barred from the first 30 minutes of the opening window: 10:00-10:30 for AC, 11:00-11:30 for non-AC
the AC 10:00 / non-AC 11:00 opening times still in force in 2025

irctcfaq.title: Tatkal Booking — IRCTC FAQ (PDF; the document carries no publication date, the retrieved file's Last-Modified header reads Thu, 21 May 2026 12:04:19 GMT)
irctcfaq.author: Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation (IRCTC)
irctcfaq.quote: 6.When I can book a tatkal E-ticket? A. Tatkal E-ticket can be booked for selected trains one day in advance excluding date of journey from the train originating station. It can be booked on the opening day from 10:00 hrs for AC class (2A/3A/CC/EC/3E) and at 11:00 hrs for Non- AC class(SL/FC/2S). e.g. if train is to depart from originating station on 2nd August, for AC class Tatkal Booking will commence at 10:00 AM and for Non AC class will Commence at 11:00 AM on 1st August. … The Tatkal Charges have been fixed as a percentage of fare at the rate of 10% of basic fare for second class and 30% of basic fare for all other classes subject to minimum and maximum as given in the table below … Sleeper: Minimum 100, Maximum 200 … AC 2 Tier: Minimum 400, Maximum 500 … 8. What are the rules for cancellation? A. No refund will be granted on cancellation of confirmed Tatkal tickets.
supports: Tatkal is sold one day in advance of the journey, excluding the date of journey
opening times 10:00 hrs AC, 11:00 hrs non-AC
the Tatkal premium the buyer pays to race: Rs 100-200 sleeper, Rs 400-500 AC 2 Tier, per passenger, over the fare
no refund on cancellation of a confirmed Tatkal ticket

unverified: Any rupee figure for the aggregate value of 'money debited but ticket not booked' transactions on IRCTC — per year, per Tatkal window, or per incident. Not stated in the IRCTC advisory or in either PIB release opened, and no other source was opened that gives one, so no such figure appears in the prose or on a card.

The hold/reservation TTL IRCTC actually applies between seat block and payment confirmation. The 2016 PIB release confirms a deliberate 'minimum payment time check' exists but gives no duration, and IRCTC publishes no expiry value; the prose therefore says the hold expires without naming a number.

The date the AC 10:00 / non-AC 11:00 Tatkal split was introduced. src/origins.json proposes 2015; no Railway Board circular establishing that date was opened. The split is only asserted here as in force in 2016 (clocksync2016 README) and in 2025 (pib2025), which is what the prose claims.

CBI prosecutions of Tatkal booking-software operators, and the 'Black TS' software named in the 2016 PIB release. An Indian Kanoon search surfaced Ajay Garg vs Central Bureau Of Investigation (Central Administrative Tribunal, Delhi, 2025) referring to software 'WINZIP' and 'NEO' used against the Tatkal system, but the judgment text itself was not opened in full, so none of it appears in the prose or on a card.
Whether IRCTC's later capacity rebuild toward 150,000 tickets/minute has shipped. Reported in trade press only; no primary or government source was opened, so it does not appear.

The effective date of the 30-minute opening-window bar on authorised agents. PIB 2025 states the restriction and its hours but attaches no date to it, unlike the 1 July and 15 July provisions in the same release; no card or the prose dates it.

Any figure for how many concurrent users actually arrive at 10:00:00, as opposed to the connection capacity provisioned for them. The 2016 release gives the provisioned ceiling (3,00,000 concurrent connections), not observed arrivals.
